raw_segments.text: Kalganov was well aware of Midia's attitude to Grushinka, and he guessed about the Pole,
too, but that did not so much interest him, perhaps did not interest him at all.
What he was interested in was Maximov.
He had come here with Maximov by chance, and he met the Poles here at the inn for the first
time in his life.
Grushinka he knew before, and had once been with someone to see her, but she had not taken
to him.
But here she looked at him very affectionately.
Before Midia's arrival, she had been making much of him, but he seemed somehow to be unmoved
by it.
He was a boy, not over twenty, dressed like a dandy, with a very charming fair-skinned
face and splendid thick fair hair.
From his fair face looked out beautiful pale blue eyes, with an intelligent and sometimes
even deep expression, beyond his age indeed, although the young man sometimes looked and
talked quite like a child, and was not at all ashamed of it, even when he was aware
of it himself.
As a rule he was very willful, even capricious, though always friendly.
Sometimes there was something fixed and obstinate in his expression.
He would look at you and listen, seeming all the while to be persistently dreaming over
something else.
Often he was listless and lazy.
At other times he would grow excited, sometimes, apparently, over the most trivial matters.
